draft.title: The warlord era
card: Yuan Shikai died in 1916. After his death, no one held power over the whole country, and China broke up into regions.
Warlords were military commanders who ruled regions with their own armies. Their power came from the soldiers they controlled, not from the central government.
The government in Beijing was weak. It had little control outside its own area, and different warlords backed it or fought over it at different times.
Warlords fought one another for land and money. They taxed local people heavily, and ordinary people suffered from the fighting and the taxes.
draft.remember: After 1916, armed regional commanders held the real power, and the national government was too weak to rule China.

a.q: Why is the period after 1916 called the warlord era?
opts: Military commanders ruled regions with their own armies
A single general ruled China through a strong government
Foreign armies took over and divided China into regions
Local councils elected by villagers ran each region
a.why: After 1916 real power lay with commanders who controlled their own armies and ruled regions. The tempting wrong option is the single general: no one held power over the whole country, and the Beijing government was weak.
a.clue: Think about who held the real power, and what backed it.

b.q: In 1920, a farming family in a region of China pays heavy taxes to the local commander, while the Beijing government does nothing about it. What does this show about China at that time?
opts: The Beijing government could not control regional rulers
The Beijing government taxed farmers to pay for its army
The commander was following orders from Beijing
The family was taxed by the Qing emperor's officials
b.why: Warlords taxed people in their regions, and the Beijing government had little control beyond its own area. So it could not stop the commander. The Qing option is wrong because the Qing had fallen in 1912.
b.clue: Ask who really held power in the region, and whether Beijing could change that.

a.best: Military commanders ruled regions with their own armies

b.best: The Beijing government could not control regional rulers
